steps: Clearances & floor protection

Set clearances to the p. 9 table (A 10.75", B 6", C 24.5", D 16.375", E 4", F 18", J 37"; letters as drawn). On a combustible floor, add a non-combustible floor shield listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1).

Minimum clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. USA floor shield: 16" out from the front and 8" out from either side of the fuel-loading door, minimum 35" x 42.125". Canada (CSA B365): ember pad 18" beyond any side with a door and 8" beyond other sides, minimum 43.5" x 52.125". No thermal hearth pad is required.
Combustion air

Balance intake air against every exhausting appliance (HRV, air handler fans, range hoods, dryers); a fresh air intake into the room is recommended. Don't connect to air distribution ductwork unless specifically approved.
Flue pipe
6" diameter, 24 MSG steel (no aluminum or galvanized), as direct as possible, every joint fastened with sheet metal screws. Never run flue pipe through an attic, roof space, closet, floor or ceiling.
Chimney

6" listed factory-built chimney to UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN), or a code-approved masonry chimney with flue liner, not shared with another appliance. At least 3ft above the roof penetration and 2ft above the highest part of the roof or any obstruction within 10ft.

Use a chimney support package through a ceiling and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall. Prefab: follow the chimney maker's instructions and buy every component (support package or wall pass through and T, fire stops, insulation shield, flashing, cap) from that maker; an interior run is recommended, with a chase around an exterior one. Masonry: have it inspected by a certified professional and cleaned first; a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, is recommended. Keep an effective vapor barrier where the chimney penetrates the exterior.
Chimney height
Minimum 15 ft vertical, stove top to termination, at 0 - 1000 ft; increase for elevation and elbows per the p. 13 table. No more than one offset (two elbows).
Fan kit power
Plug the fan kit's three-prong grounded plug directly into a properly grounded receptacle. Don't remove the grounding prong or route the cord in front of or under the stove.
Mobile home requirements
Outside air kit plus fan kit or rear shield (fit the kits first), double wall close clearance flue pipe, roof exit only; fasten the stove to the floor with the tie-downs from the outside air kit.
Install the base kit
Fit the S.Z2613 leg kit or S.Z3903 pedestal kit before connecting to the chimney. Lean the stove back with cardboard inside the firebox to support the bricks.

Leg kit (3/4" wrench): position each leg and leg plate (flanges up, away from leg) parallel to the base edges, fasten with the kit hardware, stand the stove up and level it with the levelling bolts.

Pedestal kit (7/16" wrench): remove the ash channel seal (1/4" nut), thread the four 1/4"-20 button head cap screws halfway into the base, remove the ash drawer, hang the pedestal on its key holes and slide it down, fully tighten all four, stand the stove up and refit the ash drawer.
Hang the door
Set the bottom door hinge hole on the bottom hinge pin, then the top; lower until the hinge surfaces meet (the door is heavy). Fit the bypass handle onto the bypass extension on the right side.
Installer notes & hand-over
Fill in dealer, installer, date installed and appliance serial number on the last page, and leave the manual with the homeowner.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
The first fire cures the paint: expect a strong odor and some smoke. Burn low for several hours and open a door or window until it clears. Paint color may change; that's normal.

  1. Check the bricks are in place. Build the fire on the bottom bricks, with no grate.
  2. Turn the thermostat to High and the fan (if you have one) off.
  3. Open the bypass, then the loading door.
  4. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front. Crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, with air gaps.
  5. Light it with the door cracked open. Stay with the stove.
  6. Once the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs, door unlatched until they catch.
  7. Latch the door. When the combustor temperature starts to climb, close the bypass. A door left open after the wood catches can make the combustor fail early.
  8. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer reads active, open the bypass and door, finish loading as far back as you can, then latch the door and close the bypass.
  9. Leave it on High until the fire is well established and the needle is active (at least 500F). Then turn it down gradually; if the needle drops to inactive, turn it back up.
Note: the manual says to turn the fan on to high when you close the bypass (step 7, p. 23), to turn it on after the initial warm-up (step 11, p. 23), and to keep it off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature (p. 19).

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Reload this way while the thermometer needle is still in the active zone. If it has dropped to inactive, use the lighting steps instead. The needle is only one clue: a nearly empty firebox or a cooling room also tell you it's time.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to High and wait a few minutes for the air flow to settle.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes.
  3. Crack the loading door open to let room air in. Give it a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If a lot of smoke spills out, close the door a little to get the draft going again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn it down.

Don't be afraid to fill it: the wood only burns at the rate the thermostat is set. Load only in the area shaded in the diagram on p. 22; loading beyond it voids the warranty. On low settings you may see very little flame. That's fine while the needle stays active.

Keep clear: the stove is hot when in use. Keep children and pets from touching it, and keep anything that can burn at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood within the clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass & fan
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

It's at the upper right rear corner. High gives the fastest burn and the most heat; turn it counterclockwise for less. Make changes gradually, because turning it too fast can make the thermostat work improperly. The minimum burn rate is set at the factory and must not be altered.

Bypass handle

It's on the right side. It opens a door inside the top of the stove so the fire's exhaust can skip the catalytic combustor while you light or reload. Pointing forward means open. To close it, turn it clockwise until it points to the back, then push down until you hear a click.

Leaving the bypass open too long can cause too much heat, extra creosote and even a run-away fire.

Fan (optional kit)

Keep it off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature. About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match it to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

Mild days (55F to 70F)

Run on High for 30 minutes after lighting or reloading, then turn down gradually. If it's too warm, burn smaller loads rather than turning the thermostat lower.

thermometer.title: Reading the catalytic thermometer
thermometer.html:
The dial on top of the stove tells you whether the catalytic combustor is working. The fire's exhaust passes through the combustor, which has to be above 500F to give a clean burn.

Active zoneworking: above 500F, often past 1000F
Inactive zonebelow 500F, not burning clean

Turn the fan off for a few minutes before you read it. If the needle falls to inactive, turn the thermostat back up and let the fire re-establish. Turning the thermostat down can make the combustor temperature climb for up to several hours. That's normal.

Keep the combustor healthy

  • Look it over at least three times each heating season.
  • Burn only dry, seasoned cord wood. Other materials can ruin it.
  • A hot fire usually cleans it best. If ash sticks to its face, wait until the stove is cool, lift off the flame shield and brush the face lightly with a soft paint brush. Never scrape it.
  • Still not reaching active after cleaning? Call your Blaze King dealer. The combustor, or the thermometer itself, may need replacing.
Note: p. 21 says to turn the fan off for about 5 minutes before you read the thermometer; pp. 32 and 38 say to leave it off for 10 minutes.

wood.title: Choosing firewood
wood.html:
This stove is made to burn natural cord wood only. Hardwood and softwood both burn well; dense hardwood weighs more per cord and burns a little slower and longer.

  • Aim for 20% moisture or lower. Split it, stack it so air reaches all of it, and keep it out of rain and snow for at least 24 months.
  • Never burn wet, green or unseasoned wood. It wastes heat and greatly increases creosote. If that buildup ignites, it can cause a chimney fire that may become a house fire and cause serious bodily harm.
  • Lots of small, very dry pieces, offcuts or pressed logs, used in excess, can overheat and damage the firebox.
  • Never burn salt-water driftwood. It corrodes the stove and voids the warranty.
  • Don't burn treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning.
  • Don't burn flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel.
  • Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each one down the middle.
  2. On each split face, take three readings: 2" from either end and in the middle, with the pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings. It's an approximate guide.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is a high burn for a while after each reload. Much of the creosote on the glass comes from moisture driven out of a fresh load. Leaving the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it to low for an overnight burn also helps.

After long stretches on a very low setting, run on High for about 30 minutes. That burns off most of the deposits.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and the glass are cool.
  • Use a soft cloth. No abrasive cleaners.
  • After any cleaner, rinse the glass well with water. Leftover cleaner bakes on and can be very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket seal is broken. Replacement glass must be 5 mm ceramic glass.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out whenever they come within one inch of the door opening. Don't remove them all: wood burns best on a bed of ashes around 1/2" thick.

  1. Make sure the fire is out and the stove is cool to the touch.
  2. Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Don't put other waste in it.
  3. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  4. If you'll bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all the cinders have cooled.

The fire poker that comes with the stove has a hook for removing the ash plug. After the last fire of the season, remove all the ash from the firebox and the ash drawer. The manual continues this section with illustrations on p. 33.

Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases that can suffocate. Hot ash in a vacuum cleaner bag can melt the vacuum and start a house fire.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
When wood burns slowly, it gives off tar and vapors that mix with moisture and condense in the cooler chimney as creosote. If creosote ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire. The hotter your fire, the less creosote builds up.

  • Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly through the heating season until you know how often they need cleaning.
  • Clean the chimney and the stove at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass before the chimney is swept so soot falls into the firebox.

If a chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat fully counterclockwise. Make sure the loading door and the bypass are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. If needed, use a fire extinguisher or a garden hose.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you're sure the chimney isn't damaged.
Keep at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, and a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows. Chimney fire damage isn't covered by the warranty.

care.title: Gaskets & seasonal care
care.html:
Do these regularly through the heating season, always with the stove cool. The glass and other surfaces stay hot long after the fire is out.

  • Look over the catalytic combustor and clean it as needed.
  • Clean behind internal baffles and check metal parts for warping.
  • Check the thermometer's calibration, the thermostat and the fans. Any thermostat or thermometer maintenance must be done by a certified installer.
  • Check all gaskets for a good seal.
  • Inspect and clean the chimney.

At the end of every season, clean out and inspect the stove. Have any problem fixed before the next season, or the warranty is void.

Door gasket paper test

  1. With the stove cool, latch the door on a piece of paper, such as a dollar bill.
  2. Pull it out. You should feel resistance.
  3. Repeat all around the door. Where it slides out easily, the door tension needs adjusting.

A gasket that is frayed, broken, hard or missing a piece must be replaced as a whole, with a gasket from your Blaze King dealer; Blaze King recommends your dealer fit it. Don't use the stove if the door gasket is missing or damaged.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
The limited warranty covers the original purchaser of a stove bought from an authorized Blaze King dealer and installed in the USA or Canada. It starts on the date of purchase and can't be transferred.

Catalytic combustor6 years: no charge for the first 3, then you pay 60%, 70% and 80% of the retail price in years 4, 5 and 6
Stove body and accessories, steel firebox parts5 years
Fan assemblies, thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
All parts and materials, paint finish included1 year

For parts covered beyond the first year, you pay part of the then-current retail cost: 20% in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4, 80% in year 5.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Blaze King dealer within 30 days of finding it, with proof and date of purchase. Your dealer makes the claim in writing.

Not covered, for example

  • Gaskets and firebrick
  • Over-firing, seen as warped plates and burnt-off paint
  • Glass breakage other than thermal breakage
  • Salt-saturated wood, driftwood, treated wood or other wrong fuel
  • Damage in transit, and removing or reinstalling the stove
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

Keep the flue pipe as direct as possible and fasten every joint with sheet metal screws. Don't install the chimney directly at the outlet; a chimney connector is required. Use a chimney support package through a ceiling and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall. Don't connect to a chimney serving another appliance (voids warranty). Recommended: double wall pipe from stove top adaptor to ceiling support box, a pair of 45 degree elbows instead of a single 90, a chase around exterior chimneys, and a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, in masonry chimneys.

specFloor.html:

Don't place an ember pad on carpet unless it is structurally supported. Blaze King does not recommend adhesive based vinyl flooring in front of the stove (thermal expansion and warping).
